$schema-note: Tier 3 of the design brief (2026-08-27) §3.1. One component contract each. A component token exists when a component needs a value the theme may change on its own, and it defaults to a tier 2 token.
$shape-note: A token whose name ends in -rgb names the tier 2 color token it defaults to; the generator emits it in both mode blocks so it follows the mode. Every other token holds a literal CSS value, normally a var() pointing at tier 2.
$scope-note: PR1 shipped the session card, the masthead nameplate, the lead image, and the two rule contracts. PR2 adds the contracts the six presets and their curated options remap: an option remaps existing tokens and NEVER adds a property name (brief §3.4), so every name a preset file mentions is declared here first. Every token here is read by a render path in apps/web/src/index.css — a token an option offers but nothing renders is a promise the interface does not keep, so a new contract lands with the rule that draws it. The two-axis schedule grid itself still lands in PR3; these values are what the row is set in either way.

session-card.$stamp-note: The Zine stamp (brief §2.4, 'Exception two'): a flat, unblurred, ink-tinted offset layer at a fixed small distance. Zero offset is the flat-block variant, which every other preset holds.
session-card.$stamp-tint-note: How much of that ink the second pass lays down. The brief calls the layer 'tinted with theme ink or the accent' and the Zine story spends the accent at full strength twice a page, never more — so a stamp on every row of a programme has to be a tint, not the full accent. Full ink is the contract default here because it is the neutral value; Zine's stamped block, the one choice that ever draws the layer, sets the tint it wants. Flat still means flat: a tint is one colour at one strength, with no blur and no gradient.
session-card.$gap-note: The gutter between the listings column and the row's text at wide viewports. At narrow ones the row is a single column and the gutter is not drawn.

nameplate.$treatment-note: The three nameplate treatments each preset ships (brief §4) move these four. The rule above the name is the double-rule treatment; the frame is the boxed and framed treatments; the alignment and the metadata placement are the layout. Metadata inside the rule-bounded nameplate block is part of the nameplate device, never an eyebrow (brief §2.4).
nameplate.$corner-mark-note: Atlas draws coordinate marks at two corners of the title block (brief §4.6). A mark states a position, so it appears only where something is being located: every other preset holds zero width and renders no mark at all.

$hero-note: The event hero keeps one content contract while each preset composes its photograph, veil, title, and the one permitted decorative mark. Hidden route and press marks keep those devices exclusive to Atlas and Zine.
$venue-map-note: The uploaded venue map (config/event.venue.map). The frame takes the picture's own shape, because the room markers sit on it at percentage coordinates and a frame wider or taller than the plan puts every marker on the wrong room. All that is set here is how tall a plan may get before it is scaled down; a preset may retune it.
$section-rule-note: The section boundary (brief §2.1): the rule, then the gap, then the head. The gap is one of the three surfaces config/theme.density reaches, so index.css multiplies it by --density-step.
$section-boundary-note: The Section boundary option (2026-09-10 record, §4) moves the two folio tokens: `inline` or `none` for whether the folio is drawn beside the head, and `end` or `margin` for where it sits — at the far end of the rule, or knocked out of the rule where the margin column opens beside the measure at lg and above. Zine and Atlas offer the first two choices only.
$page-note: The hybrid page shell (brief §6.1, §6.2). A system page's composable sections sit at --page-section-gap from what comes before them, and a ruled directory row is padded at --page-row-pad-block. Both are what the `density` layout variant moves: tight, comfortable, and loose remap them in index.css, and a page that states no density keeps the preset's own.
$stage-note: The stage and the measure (2026-09-10 vocabulary expansion). --stage-max is the frame: the header, the navigation, the schedule grid, the directories, the logo wall, the footer, and every section head run to it. --measure-text is the text measure: a paragraph, a list, a rich text block, a stat description, or an FAQ answer never exceeds it. Both default to the tier 2 stage family, and a style retunes either one in its preset file where its story asks: a broadsheet may run wider, a zine narrower. Neither is a fixed width. index.css reads them as a maximum inline size, and the margin column beside the measure opens only at lg and above.

folio-rule.$struck-note: A rule above the folio as well as below it is Zine's struck folio: the typewriter section break of a photocopied programme. Plain text plus rules, never a chip.

$schedule-note: The schedule presentation variants (brief §4, visual stories part 6c) and the grid itself (§2.1 'Grid schedule'). The agenda number is real sequence data, never zero-padded (brief §2.4).
$schedule-forward-note: The one expressive moment on the public site (brief §2.2): a track column comes forward on a user action. The state is a TINT of the column's ground, which lands in both motion settings; the lift is the motion, and index.css draws it only under a no-preference query. The other columns are never dimmed, so the page is readable at every frame. --schedule-trace-width is Atlas's traced line — the forward column's cells connect down the sheet — and it is zero everywhere else, which paints nothing at all.
$back-issue-note: The back issue (brief §2.1): a past day, or a past event, drops to the archive tokens, gains the "Back issue" folio, and loses its live controls. NOTHING IS HIDDEN. The device REDUCES a palette rather than introducing one: inside a back issue the accents resolve to the archive ink, which is the same text-secondary the contrast test already measures on both grounds, so an archive is quieter without ever being less readable.
$plate-note: The Field Guide botanical plate (brief §4.5): a framed drawing with a hairline border and a plate number in the folio style. A plate is drawn linework and never a hero image. The frame is a DOUBLE hairline, drawn as a border plus an outline at the same width. Zero frame and zero pad is the device off: the wrapper then adds no rule, no space, and no reflow, which is what every preset but Field Guide holds.

plate.$number-note: The plate number is real sequence data — day three is PLATE III — never a decorative zero-padded number (brief §2.4). `none` keeps it out of the document and out of the accessibility tree in every preset that is not a plate book.

$specimen-label-note: The Field Guide specimen label (brief §4.5): a small ruled block stating a name, a date, and a place. It carries session metadata and speaker credit lines, it sits below or beside the title it labels, and it is never a chip and never takes a pill radius. Zero rule width, zero padding, and a hidden key is the device off: the block is then the plain caption line it replaced.
$map-grid-note: The Atlas map grid (brief §4.6): a faint coordinate grid behind a section, held below the hairline contrast level, with pointer-events: none. Zero size turns it off.
$route-mark-note: The Atlas route mark (brief §4.6): the line letter in the heading face inside a survey-drawn shape, always with the line's name beside it. A route mark is never a coloured pill, and colour is never the only signal.
$callout-note: Zine's handwritten callout (brief §4.3). --callout-font is a component token, not a fifth semantic role (§3.1, §3.2): one callout per page, real copy, at one fixed angle. A client may point it at var(--font-heading) and drop the script face. Every other preset holds the heading face and a zero angle.
$marginalia-note: The drawn pen marks (Zine) and the pencil line (Field Guide). Its own on/off control, independent of the block variant, and off by default in both presets. A mark never lands on a single word inside a headline, which keeps the system clear of the banned headline-underline trick (brief §2.4).
$wave-2-note: The text, feedback and input devices of the vocabulary expansion (2026-09-10 record, §3), wave 2. Every contract below is read by one rule set in apps/web/src/index.css and drawn by one component, and a style remaps it in its preset file where its story differs. A contract note says why a device is the same everywhere when no style remaps it. An ink a style may move is a non-rgb token holding an rgb(var()) value, because a preset remap lands in the root block and a mode block would outrank it.
$definition-list-note: Term and description pairs (record §3.1): venue, dates, format, room. A real <dl>, ruled between pairs. This is the answer to a non-numeric fact (issue 234): a fact is a term and a description, never a stat block. The term is set in the data face by default; Zine and Field Guide move it to the mono face, Broadsheet sets it in italic, and Atlas sets it in small caps.
$pull-quote-note: A quoted sentence from a speaker or a session, with its attribution (record §3.1). One per page at most. The TEXT is the callout device: PullQuote renders its sentence through Callout.jsx, so the face, the size, the ink and the angle come from the callout contract and Zine's handwritten line is the same element as every other style's quote. What this contract holds is the frame around the sentence: the rules above and below, the rule at the inline start, the large opening mark, the alignment, and the attribution's face. The Quote device option group in each preset remaps both contracts.
$timeline-note: Dated entries in order (record §3.1): past editions, key dates, milestones. An ordered list with a spine down the leading edge and a tick per entry. It is the same spine the updates feed draws: .update-feed__entry reads these tokens too, so the two cannot drift apart. The numbers are years and dates, never sequence ornaments: the list renders no counter and nothing zero-padded. Zine and Broadsheet thicken the spine, Atlas draws a station stop on it, and Field Guide lengthens the tick.
$progress-note: How much of a set of tasks is done (record §3.2): a native <progress> with the fraction stated beside it, "3 of 5 done". <meter> is not used: it measures a quantity in a range, not completion. Never a ring. The track sits inside a hairline on the alternate ground and the fill is the accent. Zine fills in toner and squares the ends, Broadsheet keeps the bar to a hairline's height, and Atlas draws the fill as a route.
$notice-bar-note: A site-wide message with a level (record §3.2): a ruled band under the header. role=status for information, role=alert for urgent. A dismiss control, remembered per browser. The level is a word and a rule weight, never a colour alone: information takes the hairline and the word "Notice", urgent takes the strong rule and the word "Urgent". The band sits on the alternate ground in most styles; Zine sets it on the page ground between strong rules and Atlas sets its word in the mono face.
$table-note: Rows and columns a reader compares (record §3.1): a real <table> with row rules, tabular figures, a sticky head, and a horizontal scroll region at narrow widths. A sortable head holds a <button> that sorts, and the <th> carries aria-sort. The Table rules option group in each preset picks hairline rows, a ruled head, or the full grid by remapping the three widths here; the head's face and case are the style's own.
$avatar-note: A person's picture, or their initials where there is none (record §3.3). Square on the brand radius, never a circle: a circular crop is a generic-template tell. Initials are set in the heading face on the alternate ground, inside a hairline frame drawn as an inset outline so the picture keeps its full size. Zine and Atlas frame it in the strong rule; Broadsheet sets the initial in the full ink.
$dropzone-note: Send a file (record §3.3): a ruled region around a real file input, a stated progress line with a <progress> element, and a sent list with a state word per file. The region's rule is the control boundary, drawn dashed at rest so an empty region reads as a place to put something, and solid while a file is held over it. Zine draws it solid and strong; Broadsheet and Field Guide keep a hairline.
$repeater-note: A short list of rows a person adds and removes (record §3.3): each row's fields labelled, one remove control per row, one add control under the list, every one on the keyboard path. Rows are ruled between, like every list in the system. Zine rules them at the strong width; the rest keep the hairline.
$count-note: A labelled figure beside the thing it counts (record §3.2): "12 saved". The figure in the mono face with tabular figures, the label always present in the data face, never a bubble. The figure sentence composes the same figures into a line of body copy: "412 registered, 38 in the last day, read at 09:14". Broadsheet sets both figures in its serif data face through the role; Zine gives the figure the bold weight.
$legend-note: Names what a marker or a count means on a page (record §3.2): one line at the head of the list, in the data face. Zine rules it above at the strong width, the way its folios are struck; Broadsheet sets it in small capitals.
$state-marker-note: "Now", "Next", "Finished" on a session row during the event (record §3.2): a word in the data face with an ink change and a rule under it. A live session takes the accent, a finished one takes the back-issue ink and the hairline. Never a pill: the word is the signal and the rule and the ink are its second and third. Zine and Atlas set the word in the mono face.
$standfirst-note: The one sentence under a heading that says what the page or session is (record §3.1). It sits below the heading, never above it, at the lead step. Each style names its face and its rule: Broadsheet and Field Guide set it in italic, Newsroom in the heading face, Zine on a strong rule, Atlas in the heading face at regular weight.
$byline-note: Who, in what role, and when (record §3.1). The byline and the dateline share one contract: both are set in the data face at the caption step, and a dateline carries the event's clock, never the reader's. Broadsheet sets both in small capitals with tracking; Zine, Atlas and Field Guide set them in the mono face.
$directory-note: The four directories (brief §5.1) on one token system. A style's Directory style option remaps these: the rule between entries, the portrait's proportion, ground and corner on the speaker shelf, and the row padding of the attendee index. The sponsor wall keeps its own logo-wall size token and the updates feed reads the timeline contract.
$long-read-note: The opening of a long read (record §3.1, brief §2.1): a drop cap, a standfirst, or plain. The Long read opening option in each preset picks one by remapping these tokens; the contract defaults are the plain opening, so a style that names nothing draws no cap. The cap's face, leading, weight, ink and lift apply only while the first letter floats (a style query in index.css), so a choice moves three tokens to turn the cap on and two to size the opening line. One drop cap per page at most, on the first paragraph of the first block of a page on the Long read template, never on a short intro and never on a card. Broadsheet and Field Guide default to the cap, Newsroom to the standfirst, Civic, Zine and Atlas to plain.
